sections.h2: Where to record a deed in Berks County
sections.html:
The Recorder of Deeds is on the third floor of the Berks County Services Center, 633 Court Street, Reading, PA 19601. Counter hours are 8 a.m. to 4 p.m., Monday through Friday, and the phone is 610-478-3380. Documents can also arrive by e-recording, by mail or over the counter.

The office does more than file deeds. It collects state and local real estate transfer taxes, affordable housing fees, judicial fees and redeterminations, records subdivision and land development plans, highway maps and real estate UCC liens, and swears in notaries. Every document recorded since the county was founded in 1752 is available as an image and index on its online search site, with original handwritten and typed books kept for 1752 to 1953.

Owners can use the Property Alert tool, a fraud protection service that tells you when something is recorded against your address.

A deed, agreement, easement, lease or order of court carries a base fee of $88.00 for up to four pages, and every added page is $4.00. The fee schedule took effect on November 14, 2025, and a Statement of Value counts as an extra page when fees are figured. The base fee includes one tax parcel, and each additional parcel is $15.00.

Berks County recording fees effective November 14, 2025

There is an extra charge to index more than 15 names on one document. Statements of Value that arrive through e-recording are charged a $0.50 per page copy fee for printing and mailing to the Department of Revenue.

The rate depends on where the house sits. The fee schedule lists 5% in the City of Reading and 2% in all other Berks municipalities. That is charged before any recording fee.

How you pay matters here. The office no longer accepts cash or personal checks for transfer tax. Overpayments of $10 or less are forfeited, and checks 180 days old or older are refused. Checks are made payable to Berks County Recorder of Deeds.

  • Ask your closing agent whether the title company will pay by company check or wire.
  • Confirm which municipality and school district appear on the deed, especially for Wyomissing Borough, where deeds must name Wyomissing or Wilson School District.
  • Read the purchase agreement to see who pays the tax, since the split is a negotiated term.

A Statement of Value is required on every deed that leaves out the full and complete value of the property, unless a family exemption applies, in which case the exemption has to be stated in the deed. It must also accompany easements and rights of way. The form is completed in duplicate under Department of Revenue rules, and it is the Pennsylvania REV-183.

The form uses the Common Level Ratio, which changes each July 1. For documents accepted from July 1, 2026 to June 30, 2027 the Berks County factor is 3.12. Since the office treats the form as an additional page, include it when you estimate fees so the check comes out exact.

Berks County is specific about format. Documents should be on white 8.5 by 11 inch paper at 20 pound weight, in a font no smaller than 10 point, with a one inch margin at the top and one inch margins on the sides and bottom. Legal size paper is no longer accepted, and light copies will not be scanned legibly, so use dark print and black ink.

  • A Property Identification Number (UPI) is required on every document that references real estate, and the grantee’s mailing address must be exact, current and legible.
  • The written amount on a deed must match the numerical amount.
  • The acknowledgment needs the state and county, date, signers, notary signature and a clear stamp with an expiration date.
  • Do not include Social Security numbers or bank or loan numbers, since the Recorder may redact or reject the document.
  • The submitter’s name and company must be typed in the Return To area, with a stamped, self-addressed envelope.

Documents received by 3:30 p.m. are generally recorded that same day and held until the next day before being returned. A document written in a foreign language has to be recorded with an English translation sworn or affirmed by the translator.

Reading is the county seat, and the Schuylkill River runs through the county, about 50 miles northwest of Philadelphia. Population is 440,072 for 2025, up 2.6% from 2020, with 172,559 housing units and 163,236 households. The owner-occupied rate is 71.3%, the median value of an owner-occupied home is $257,300, and median gross rent is $1,181.

The submitter decides where the recorded document goes, because the office requires a postage-paid, addressed envelope with each one. Title companies and attorneys often address it to themselves and forward it, and others address it to the new owner. If a copy never shows, check with the closing agent first, then request a copy from the Recorder.

Certified copies ordered online are $10.00 per document, regular copies from the website are 50 cents a page, and copies made in the office, other than your own home’s deed, are also 50 cents a page. Credit card payments add a processor fee that is not a county charge. After a mortgage payoff, the lender has 60 days to file the satisfaction, and Pennsylvania lenders do not hold deeds, so no new deed will arrive.

sections.h2: Changing names and selling for cash
sections.html: To add or remove a name on a deed, a new deed has to be prepared and recorded. An attorney can often prepare and file it, and the office line is 610-478-3380. For a cash sale, the recording rules do not change: the deed still needs the right paper, a Statement of Value if the price is not stated, the UPI and a transfer tax payment the office will accept. What disappears is the lender, so the title company can usually send the deed in right after signing. Ask for the recorded copy and keep it.

faqs.q: What is the base fee to record a deed in Berks County?
faqs.a: The base fee is $88.00 for up to four pages and one tax parcel. Every extra page is $4.00 and each extra parcel is $15.00, under the schedule effective November 14, 2025.

faqs.q: What is the Berks County transfer tax on a home sale?
faqs.a: It is 5% in the City of Reading and 2% in every other Berks municipality. The office no longer takes cash or personal checks for it.

faqs.q: How do I add or remove a name on my Berks County deed?
faqs.a: A new deed has to be prepared and recorded. An attorney can often file it too, and the office phone is 610-478-3380.

faqs.q: What is the Berks County Common Level Ratio for 2026 to 2027?
faqs.a: The factor is 3.12 for documents accepted from July 1, 2026 to June 30, 2027. It changes every July 1 and goes on the Statement of Value.

faqs.q: Does the Berks County Recorder record military discharge papers?
faqs.a: Yes, recording a DD-214 and the military ID card are free. Bring the original discharge papers if you have not recorded them before.
